H1_primary.claim: M0 (label A) pre-onset catches exceed the budget-preserving regime-matched null
H1_primary.decision: supported if p < alpha; reported either way

P1.claim: at H = 1440: GBM - M0 standard AUC > 0 and GBM - M0 pre-onset AUC < 0
P1.inference: shared 500 x 7-day block bootstrap on the common minutes; read supported if both intervals exclude 0 in the predicted directions, contradicted if either excludes 0 in the other direction, inconclusive otherwise; within-regime pre-onset AUC also reported; a difference is undefined in a draw when either AUC has no positive or no negative minute, and an interval is reported only when the difference is defined in at least 80% of draws, otherwise it is undefined and P1 is inconclusive; the number of defined draws is reported

P2.claim: at H = 240: M0 catches more events before onset than GBM under the frozen alerts
P2.inference: exact one-sided McNemar on discordant events; event counts reported; inconclusive if fewer than 10 events are caught pre-onset by either method; the paired difference in pre-onset catch rate (M0 minus GBM) is reported with a 95% interval from a calendar-month block bootstrap over events (10000 draws, same defined-draw rule as P1); the interval describes the size of the effect and does not decide P2

S1: M0 in-progress catches under the same null (nominal p)
S2: M1, M2, M3 on both endpoints under the same null; Holm across the three methods within each endpoint
S3: labels B, B2, C for M0 and GBM: pre-onset catches under the same null; exact one-sided McNemar (variant better than A) on pre-onset catches, Holm within method
descriptive: stage decomposition of missed events (signal / window / cooldown / budget) with the Python replay
lead times of pre-onset catches per event (saved), with the median and the shares of catches at least [30, 60] minutes before the onset and within 60 minutes of it
null-draw audit: share of alerts placed in their own volatility decile, in the nearest decile, or left in place; monthly-count, cap, budget and cooldown checks on the first 50 draws

data coverage by month: minutes on the grid, minutes missing from the archives, invalid minutes; events whose 240-min warning window crosses the period start are excluded by the event rule and counted
all alerts and events listed with timestamps (no prices)

evaluation_period.descriptive_update: the same analysis at 24 months, reported as descriptive
evaluation_period.events: breach in [start + 240 min, end - 4 min): the 5-close confirmation needs 4 closes after the breach, and the archives of the period end at end - 1 min; monthly archives only, SHA-256 verified; no API data in the confirmatory run

exclusions: none; minutes with missing archive data are NaN and cannot host alerts or events; exchange incidents are reported, not excluded

failure_rules.bootstrap: draws in which a quantity is undefined are dropped from its interval; if fewer than 80% of draws define it, the interval is undefined and the reading is inconclusive
failure_rules.no_events: if no evaluation event exists, H1, S1, S2, S3 and P2 are reported as not testable; nothing is extended or re-drawn
failure_rules.no_resampling_or_extension: the seed, the number of draws and the evaluation period are fixed here and are not changed after any result is seen
failure_rules.null_distribution: the null p-value is defined for any number of events (including zero catches); it is never re-drawn
failure_rules.null_placement: decile search (same, then nearest deciles, 64 candidates each), then a scan of every minute of the month for one that keeps both the 240-min distance from the original and the cooldown against alerts already placed; an alert with no feasible minute keeps its time and the draw is kept; the numbers of such alerts and of the cooldown violations they create are reported over all draws (expected to be zero)
failure_rules.undefined_auc: an AUC with no positive or no negative minute is NaN; a NaN point estimate makes P1 inconclusive

secondary_event_definitions.P1_H1440: price_only_catalog with H = 1440: peak = highest close in the 1440 minutes before the breach, breach = close <= 0.96 x that peak, sustained 5 closes, 1440-min refractory; onset = first close after the peak at least 1% below it; per-minute label = breach 30-240 min ahead; in-progress positive = at or after the onset of the event that makes the minute positive; evaluation minutes = valid minutes in the period ending 245 min before its end with finite 24h RV, both M0 and GBM scores finite; RV deciles and 7-day blocks over those minutes
